scope: Read-only re-review of the two day-two Emet veEmunah modules (prayerbook_for_the_new_year_second_day-heidenheim-1965-he/emet_veemunah.xml and prayerbook_for_the_new_year_second_day-marmorstein-1965-en/emet_veemunah.xml). Checked them against emet_veemunah_units.json, emet_veemunah_text_qa.json, approved working/s10.json, primary/s11.json, s10_source_reading_approval.json and s9_s11_source_reading_approval.json. Also re-reviewed draft_prayers.py and test_marmorstein_day_two_excerpts.py, and checked that all three findings in the earlier changes_required review (independent/emet_veemunah_encoding/response.json) are fixed. I left that file untouched; I only had read access. Not done: I did not look at images or rerun tests or schema validation. I did not search siddur.jsonl, because it is 1 MB and I had no search tool. I relied on the earlier review's check that the six part URNs match the accepted day-one modules. I did not reread SCAN_DIGITIZATION_INSTRUCTIONS.md or JLPTEI-3.md beyond what the earlier review covered. I could not find the whole-word DivineName QA regex in the files I was pointed to, so I checked every j:divineName in both modules by hand instead. No full-scan, whole-batch, service-condition, expanded-spine or export acceptance.

prior_findings_closure.evidence: בַּחַיִּים is now plain text in units.json:30 and in the Hebrew module at line 39. All four j:divineName elements in the Hebrew module are whole-word tokens: יְיָ (opening), יְהֹוָה (Exod 15:11), יְהֹוָה (Exod 15:18), יְיָ (Jer 31:11) and יְיָ (seal). That is five elements in total, each a single complete word bounded by spaces or by the start of the seg. I could not verify the claim that all other generated day-two projects were scanned with the new regex, because that QA code was not in the files I was given.

draft_prayers.py:108-121 now carries current_page across parts. append_prayer_content (61-92) takes the page from both plain-content and quotation-content page breaks, and finds the seg@facs start page by skipping leading whitespace and page breaks, the same way the range branch does. This is covered by test_prayer_quotation_source_tracks_a_preceding_page_break (tests:82-92).
draft_prayers.py:66-69 requires exactly the keys {urn, chapter, verse, content} and requires the urn to end with /chapter/verse. The mismatch is tested at tests:93-95.

findings.summary: The quotation URN check does not check the bible prefix and does not rule out ranges.
findings.detail: The endswith('/ch/v') test stops chapter and verse from disagreeing with the URN. It still accepts a non-Bible URN that happens to end the same way, or a range URN whose last component matches, such as .../15/10-/15/11. Nothing in this recipe triggers either case.

findings.summary: The QA record does not say that the whole-word DivineName check was run.
findings.detail: The record lists exact_source_words, parts, paragraphs and quotations. It has no field for the new divine-name token check, which is the check that would have caught the original finding 1. A later reader cannot tell from the record that the check passed.
findings.suggested_change: Add something like divine_names_whole_word: true, plus the list of tokens, and say which script ran the check.

findings.summary: The first Hebrew paragraph ends with a trailing space.
findings.detail: The space separates parts in the recipe and is left behind when the next part opens a new paragraph. Under normal whitespace handling it changes nothing in the text. Mentioned only for tidiness.

verified_without_issue: Hebrew text: every word, vowel point, meteg, dagesh, maqaf and punctuation mark in all 5 paragraphs matches approved s10.json blocks 4-8 exactly. That includes the '.' after עֲלֵיהֶם, כֻלָּם, וְאָמְרוּ and מִמֶּֽנּוּ, and the ':' marks. No normalization was applied. The Numbers 15 continuation and the instruction יש לצרף אלהיכם לאמת… are correctly left out and kept for the service spine.
English text: matches s11.json prayer blocks 3-9 exactly, in 4 paragraphs. None of the Hebrew cues (אמת, מי, מלכותך, ונאמר) appear.

Paragraphs vs. alignment: the Hebrew has 5 paragraphs and the English has 4, each following its own source independently of the six alignment parts. /opening carries across the first Hebrew paragraph break (the urn-less part with new_paragraph=true adds no milestone). /mosheh comes inside Hebrew paragraph 2 just before מֹשֶׁה, and inside English paragraph 1 just before 'Moses'. Both languages open the six parts in the same order. The last paragraph ends with a bare prayer-part terminator.

Bounded quotations: exodus/15/11, exodus/15/18 and jeremiah/31/11 each have a chapter milestone (n only), a verse milestone with a canonical corresp, a seg@source with per-quotation facs, and bare verse and chapter terminators. The Jeremiah terminators come before the unrelated text בָּרוּךְ / 'Blessed'. No quotation claims a whole chapter. jeremiah/31/11 is correct for canonical numbering (the earlier review checked this against versification.py).

Facsimiles: pb ed=1965 n=4. The Hebrew points to Archive leaf n9 (scan 10) and the English to n10 (scan 11). Every quotation seg's facs matches its own language's leaf. biblScope is 4-4, the ptr is the edition-qualified #day_two_source_bibl, and the idno uses urn@project.

Code: excerpt_header (42-58) is called the same way by the Bible branch, so Bible behaviour is unchanged. The prayer branch rejects an empty parts list, a prayer that does not start with a canonical part, and duplicate part URNs, all before writing. The stale-hash and validation guards still apply because everything is built before write_documents. The new synthetic tests cover parts and paragraphs, quotation terminators, paragraph continuation, preceding-page-break provenance, and inconsistent coordinates. I did not rerun them; the QA record says 41 tests and 19 subtests passed.
